Algorithm for Computing the LCM

ArithmeticAlgorithmsInvariants
Game: Raise the smallest number until all the numbers match — then you have their LCM.
How to play: Edit the starting numbers, then press Step or Run. Reset returns to the start.

Look for the math

A tiny rule, repeated, finds the least common multiple without factoring anything.

The rule

At each step take the smallest current number and add to it its original value. For 6, 10, 15 the first few states are (12, 10, 15), (12, 20, 15), (12, 20, 30), and eventually all three become 30 — their LCM.

Why it stops at the right number

Every value stays a multiple of its original number, so a common value is a common multiple. No value can jump past the true LCM: it would have to cross the multiple that another value is approaching, contradicting that the crossed value was smallest. Hence the first common value is the least common multiple. The logic test checks 600 random sets: the loop always terminates at the value given by the gcd formula, with no value ever exceeding it.

Try numbers that share no factors, like 7 and 11. How many steps does it take?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
